court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: Family Court, Madurai, H.M.O.P.No.425 of 2017 and H.M.O.P.No.802 of 2016
facts_of_case: Marriage between the parties was solemnised on 09.12.2012. The husband sought divorce under Section 13(1)(i-a) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, while the wife sought restitution of conjugal rights under Section 9 of the Act. The trial court dismissed the husband's petition and allowed the wife's petition.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party alleging cruelty to prove it.
legal_principles.held: Though in the petition he claimed that immediately after marriage they started living at a rented house, Maduvinagar, Guindy, in cross-examination he admitted that they first lived at Door No.1, Jeeva Nagar, 1st Cross Street, Pallikaranai, and that the Ooty trip and certain intermediate stays were not disclosed as pleaded.

legal_principles.principle: A party's financial grievance is not a proven ground of cruelty unless substantiated with evidence.
legal_principles.held: The husband admitted in cross-examination that he had not produced any document to substantiate his claim that he spent Rs.12,00,000/- for the marriage or that he borrowed Rs.7,00,000/- for that purpose.

outcome.final_order: The appeals are disposed of by this common judgment.
